cattle noun

also head of cattle, cattle low, cattle bellow

classical

Liv. 1.7: inde cum āctae bovēs mūgīssent (Lewis & Short s.v. mūgiō)
Traupman 288

bovēs, boum m. pl.

plural of bōs; dative and ablative bōbus or būbus · Declension on Wiktionary

cattle, oxen and cows

The plural of bōs, ox or cow (see ox, cow). Cattle as livestock in general is pecus, pecoris n.; a single head of cattle, one beast of the herd, is pecus, pecudis f. (Lewis & Short; see livestock).

Other words

  • pecus, pecoris n. — cattle, livestock (collectively)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Varr. R. R. 2.1.13: būbulum pecus, horned cattle (Lewis & Short); Traupman 288 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Collective: the herd or flock as a whole (Lewis & Short, opposing it to pecus, pecudis, a single head).

Examples

  • Bovēs mūgiunt.

    The cattle are lowing.Traupman 288

See also ox, cow, livestock, herd, moo.
